claims.text: Neural networks trained on existing thermodynamic data can predict melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
Neural networks trained on existing thermodynamic data can predict enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
Neural networks trained on existing thermodynamic data can predict entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
Neural networks trained on existing thermodynamic data can predict volume changes at melting for high-entropy alloys.
Neural networks trained on existing thermodynamic data can predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The neural-network approach can make these predictions across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The neural-network approach determines the target thermodynamic properties efficiently.
Machine-learning algorithms identify patterns and relationships in training data that correlate with thermodynamic properties.
Patterns learned from existing thermodynamic data enable predictions for new alloy compositions.
Predictions will have a mean absolute error below 5% relative to experimental values.
The approach applies over varying high-entropy-alloy compositions and temperatures.
The approach may not generalize beyond high-entropy alloys.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality of the neural-network training data.
Prediction accuracy depends on the compositional and thermodynamic range represented in the training data.
Current methods for determining the relevant thermodynamic properties may lack accuracy.
Current methods for determining the relevant thermodynamic properties may lack efficiency.
Deviation of predictions from experimental measurements by more than 10% is designated as a falsifying result.
